findings.title: Checkpoint timing after batch completion
findings.description: A restart-safe checkpoint is required immediately after the nightly batch ends.

evidence.quote: When the backup agent, finishes the nightly batch it must record a restart-safe checkpoint before any further retention jobs begin.

findings.machine_interpretation: Batch completion and checkpointing are ordered steps that must not reverse after restart.
findings.recommendation_level1: Document the required checkpoint boundary after batch completion.
findings.scope_rationale: This matters to time assurance because a missed checkpoint after a batch can replay retention against stale state.

findings.title: Cross-terminal inventory deltas
findings.description: Inventory deltas from one terminal cannot be applied to another without reconciliation.

evidence.quote: Each warehouse keeps a local inventory clock, and stock deltas computed on one floor terminal may be applied to a second terminal only after reconciliation.

findings.machine_interpretation: Local inventory clocks are not interchangeable until reconciliation completes.
findings.recommendation_level1: Require an explicit reconciliation step before applying cross-terminal deltas.
findings.scope_rationale: This matters to time assurance because unsynchronized inventory clocks can accept out-of-order stock updates.

findings.title: Archive cutoff rejection
findings.description: Imports must fail when the retained index is older than the declared archive cutoff.

evidence.quote: If context’s retained index is older than archive’s declared cutoff the loader must refuse the import.

findings.machine_interpretation: Archive import eligibility is a cutoff comparison against the retained index age.
findings.recommendation_level1: Reject imports that violate the declared archive cutoff.
findings.scope_rationale: This matters to time assurance because accepting an older retained index can revive expired archive rows.
